title: Cross-functional Onboarding: Field Guide for ICs and Managers
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

Purpose:
This field guide standardizes cross-functional onboarding at Redwood Inference for individual contributors (ICs) and their managers. It balances fast technical contribution with relationship-building across product, infra, and platform teams. Use this guide to reduce time-to-impact and to create consistent evidence for 30/60/90 performance conversations.

Scope:
- New IC hires (engineer, data scientist, product designer) joining teams that must interact with 2+ partner teams within 90 days.
- Applies to remote, hybrid, and on-site hires.
- Does NOT replace role-specific training (see team-specific learning plans).

Summary of outcomes (first 90 days):
1) Role clarity: written success criteria co-signed by manager and IC.
2) Cross-team relationships: at least 2 stable working relationships outside the home team.
3) Contribution: first meaningful change merged (bugfix, perf improvement, doc, small feature) within 30 days and demonstrable roadmap impact by day 90.
4) Feedback rhythm: established 1:1 cadence and documented checkpoints.

Owners & responsibilities:
- People Operations: maintain this guide, onboarding templates, and centralized access to accounts.
- Hiring Manager: role success criteria, 30/60/90 plan, weekly 1:1s, pairing schedule.
- Buddy (assigned peer): daily practical support first 30 days, codebase walkthroughs, culture norms.
- Cross-team sponsor: intro to partner teams and initial context for collaboration.

Pre-Day 1 (Checklist for hiring manager, to be completed at least 3 business days before start):
- Create the 30/60/90 draft and share with new hire.
- Grant core system access (Slack, email, repo read, CI viewer, dev sandbox).
- Book Day 1 calendar blocks: Welcome, Admin walk-through, Team kickoff, Buddy pairing session.
- Add new hire to team channel(s) and shared docs; create "new-hire" folder with links.
- Assign a buddy with explicit time blocks for first-week pairing.

Day 1 — Orientation flow (sample agenda):
1) Welcome (30m): Manager + People Ops overview, key contacts, office logistics.
2) Admin & Security (30m): HR forms, laptop provisioning, MFA/KMS brief.
3) Team Kickoff (45m): team mission, active projects, current blockers.
4) Buddy pairing (60m): codebase tour + first tiny task assignment.
5) Slack introductions and documentation handover.

Days 2–7 — Rapid ramping checklist:
- Complete security and compliance training (KMS/HSM basics if relevant).
- Run local dev environment and pass smoke tests.
- Deliver the first tiny task (e.g., doc update, lint fix, simple unit test).
- Schedule cross-team intro calls with 2 partner teams.
- Manager: review initial progress and adjust 30-day goals.

Weeks 2–4 — Integration activities and goals:
- Pair with at least 2 team members on production code reviews.
- Join recurring cross-team syncs and add one agenda item to contribute.
- Demonstrate ownership of a small scoped deliverable (tracked in ticketing system).
- Begin weekly upward feedback (new hire -> manager) during 1:1s.

First 90 days — Success metrics & evidence (use during performance check-ins):
- 30-day milestone: environment running, first merged change, active cross-team intros. Evidence: PR link, screenshot of passing local tests, cross-team meeting notes.
- 60-day milestone: feature or improvement with clear owner / acceptance criteria. Evidence: ticket link, demo recording, stakeholder sign-off.
- 90-day milestone: measurable impact (latency improvement, reduced CI time, user-facing bug elimination, or product metric uplift). Evidence: before/after metrics, post-implementation notes, retrospective doc.

Manager pairing schedule (recommended):
- Week 0–2: 3x 60-minute paired sessions (codebase, infra, ship process).
- Week 3–6: 1x 60-minute paired deep-dive per week focusing on domain knowledge.
- Week 7–12: 1x 30-minute alignment + 1 targeted pairing session every other week.

Feedback & performance conversation cadence:
1) Weekly 1:1s (30–45m) for the first 90 days. Topics: unblockers, task prioritization, well-being, learning plan progress.
2) 30/60/90 written checkpoint (IC updates the doc; manager attaches evidence).
3) Formal 90-day review: manager provides written summary, strengths, growth areas, and a development plan.
4) Invite peer reviewers from partner teams to the 60- and 90-day checkpoints (no more than 3).

Hiring team handoff checklist (what recruiting should provide to manager on offer acceptance):
- Candidate packet: resume, interview loop feedback summary, take-home or PR sample, and scoring notes.
- Compliance notes: visa or background check requirements.
- Start logistics: confirmed start date, hardware needs, seniority calibration.

Cross-team onboarding norms (agreements to set during first 2 weeks):
- Communication: expected response times (Slack: 24 hours for FYI, 4 hours for blockers during working hours).
- Meeting practice: agenda + 24-hr pre-read for cross-team design reviews; timeboxed meetings (max 60m).
- Ownership handoffs: ticket-based transfer with acceptance criteria and rollback plan.

Escalation & runbook access:
- New hires must be given read access to production runbooks and incident contacts within the first 7 days.
- If needed, manager escalates access delays to People Ops within 48 hours.

Templates (appendix) — copy into new-hire folder and personalize:
- 30/60/90 Plan (one-page):
| Timeframe | Objective | Evidence | Success criteria |
|-----------|-----------|----------|------------------|
| 0–30d | Onboard & ship first change | PR link, buddy notes | Environment working, PR merged |
| 31–60d | Deliver owned improvement | Ticket link, demo | Feature accepted by stakeholders |
| 61–90d | Measured impact & roadmap fit | Metrics, retrospective | Impact validated or roadmap adoption |

- Sample 1:1 agenda (first 8 weeks):
  - Quick wins / blockers (5m)
  - Priorities for the week (10m)
  - Learning & growth check (10m)
  - Cross-team coordination items (5m)
  - Feedback to manager (5m)

Manager checklist for evidence capture (so reviews are objective):
- Link to PR(s) with description of contribution.
- Demonstration video or staging demo link.
- Performance metrics or before/after measurements.
- Peer feedback snippets (1–2 lines) from partner teams.

Operational notes & constraints:
- Security: every hire touching customer data needs completed Data Handling training before any access to customer PII.
- Access windows: depending on region and KMS, approvals for certain key management are expected to take 2–5 business days. Plan accordingly.
- Role variance: for technical ICs joining cross-functional product pods, expect additional product onboarding (PM-led) in weeks 2–6.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Failure: no cross-team introductions. Mitigation: manager arranges a block of 30-minute intro slots within week 1 and sets calendar invites.
- Failure: new hire cannot run local environment. Mitigation: buddy-led pairing session with a recorded environment setup video and runbook.
- Failure: access delays blocking work. Mitigation: People Ops escalation channel with explicit SLA: respond within 24 hours, resolution within 72 hours.

Ownership, review cycle & updates to this guide:
- Owner: People Ops (Maya Chen).
- Review cadence: annual review or sooner after major tooling/process changes.
- Feedback channel: submit improvements to /confluence/people-ops via the doc comments or email people-ops@redwood.com.

Appendix: sample 30/60/90 (text) — to be copied into hire folder:
- 30 days: Run the full test suite locally, fix or triage two non-critical bugs, and merge doc or lint change.
- 60 days: Own a small feature end-to-end (design to rollout) with stakeholder demo.
- 90 days: Propose a measurable improvement and run an experiment or rollout with metrics for evaluation.

Related resources:

- Code review and PR guidelines (eng-developer-experience/docs-site)
